summary: Hard for an agent that reads email: reading or changing mail uses restricted scopes, which need Google's verification plus a third-party security assessment every 12 months. If your agent only sends email, gmail.send is a sensitive scope, which needs verification but no security assessment.
timeToProduction: About 1–2 weeks with gmail.send only; several weeks or more to read mail
cost: Free with gmail.send only; reading mail adds a yearly security assessment, paid to the assessor (Google charges nothing)

gates.title: Any Google account can register the app
Testing mode: 100 test users, and logins expire after 7 days
gates.what: Until you publish, only listed test users (up to 100) can connect, and each authorization expires 7 days after consent.
gates.where: Google Auth Platform > Audience. You add test users.
gates.todo: Build and test in Testing, then publish and verify before real users connect.

gates.title: Google must verify Gmail scopes before the public can connect
gates.what: Sensitive scopes like gmail.send need verification (typically 3–5 business days). Restricted scopes, needed to read mail, need verification that can take several weeks, plus a security assessment if the data passes through your servers.
gates.where: Google Auth Platform: Branding first, then the OAuth Verification Center. You submit.
gates.todo: Publish your branding, then submit data access verification with a scope justification and a demo video.

gates.title: Workspace admins can block your app
gates.what: A Workspace admin has the final say on which apps reach their organization's data. If your app requests a restricted service the admin hasn't trusted, their users can't add it.
gates.where: Google Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls. The customer's admin acts here, not you.
gates.todo: Ask business customers' Workspace admins to mark your app as trusted.

gates.title: No paid tier needed for standard Gmail API use
Restricted scopes: security assessment every 12 months
gates.what: To keep restricted scopes, the app must be reverified and pass a security assessment at least every 12 months.
gates.where: Google emails you when it's due. You arrange the assessment with an approved assessor.
gates.todo: Keep the project's contact emails current and plan the yearly assessment.

requirements.text: A Google account that is Owner or Editor on a Google Cloud project
A domain you own, verifiable in Google Search Console
A public home page, and a privacy policy on the same domain
A budget for a third-party security assessment if you need restricted scopes (Google itself charges nothing)

steps.text: In your Google Cloud project, open Google Auth Platform and set the audience to External.
steps.why: External lets any Google account use the app. Internal limits it to your own Workspace organization, and anyone else gets an org_internal error. An app for outside users needs External.

steps.text: Fill in the branding fields: app name, logo, support email, home page and privacy policy links.
steps.why: These appear on the consent screen.
steps.detail: The home page must be public; the privacy policy must be on the same domain and linked from the consent screen.

steps.text: Verify ownership of your domain in Google Search Console.
steps.detail: Use a Google account that is Owner or Editor on the Cloud project.

steps.text: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes your features need and declare them.
steps.why: Sensitive scopes need verification only; restricted scopes also need a security assessment if data passes through your servers.
steps.detail: Sending only: gmail.send (sensitive). Reading, labelling or archiving mail: restricted scopes.

steps.text: Create an OAuth client ID of type Web application, with your redirect URIs.
steps.detail: If your app has both AI agent workflows and regular user features, Google asks for a separate OAuth client for each.

steps.text: Add test users and connect your own account.
steps.why: In Testing, only listed test users (up to 100) can connect.
steps.detail: Test logins expire after 7 days, so reconnect weekly while testing.

steps.text: Click Publish app to move the project to In production.
steps.why: Until you're verified, users see an unverified-app screen and the app is capped at 100 new users for the project's whole lifetime.

steps.text: Click Verify Branding, then Publish branding once it shows Ready to publish.
steps.detail: Review typically takes 2–3 business days. Publish within 7 days of a passing result, or run the check again.

steps.text: Write the scope justification and the demo video script.
steps.why: Google asks for a detailed justification and a video demonstration for sensitive scopes.

steps.text: Record the demo video and upload it to YouTube as Unlisted.
steps.detail: Show the consent flow users will see, in English.

steps.text: Submit data access verification in the OAuth Verification Center.
steps.why: Your branding must be published first.

steps.detail: Typically 3–5 business days for sensitive scopes; restricted scopes can take several weeks.

steps.text: If you use restricted scopes, complete the security assessment with a Google-approved assessor.
steps.detail: Repeat it at least every 12 months; Google emails you when it's due.

blockers.problem: Users see an unverified-app screen and sign-ups stop at 100.
blockers.fix: Finish verification for every sensitive and restricted scope you request. The cap covers the project's whole lifetime and can't be reset.

blockers.problem: Users in a company Workspace can't add your app.
blockers.fix: Their admin must mark your app as trusted in the Admin console's API controls.

blockers.problem: Test users get signed out after 7 days.
blockers.fix: That's the Testing limit. Reconnect weekly until the app is published.
The passing result wasn't published within 7 days. Run brand verification again, then publish.

blockers.problem: You can't request data access verification.

couldNotVerify: Time to test, hands-on effort and the overall timeline are estimates; Google publishes review times for each stage but no end-to-end figure.
What the security assessment costs: each approved assessor sets its own price.
Charges for Gmail API usage above the free limits: Google says billing details come later in 2026.

claims.statement: Restricted Gmail scopes give wide access to user data and require restricted scope OAuth App Verification.
claims.quote: These scopes provide wide access to Google user data and require restricted scope OAuth App Verification

claims.statement: Sensitive Gmail scopes require additional OAuth App Verification.
claims.quote: These scopes provide access to specific Google user data that users authorize for your app. They require additional OAuth App Verification

claims.statement: gmail.send is a sensitive scope.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Cloud Help: OAuth App Verification FAQ
claims.quote: To use the Gmail API and continue with the verification process, you will need to migrate off SMTP protocol and use the sensitive https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send scope instead.

claims.statement: If you store or transmit restricted scope data on servers, you must go through a security assessment.
claims.quote: If you store restricted scope data on servers (or transmit), then you must go through a security assessment.

claims.statement: To keep restricted scopes, apps must be reverified and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months.
claims.quote: As mentioned previously, to keep access to any verified restricted scopes, apps must be reverified for compliance and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months after your assessor's Letter of Assessment (LOA) approval date.

claims.statement: Restricted scope verification can take several weeks.
claims.quote: For this reason, the restricted scopes verification process can potentially take several weeks to complete.

claims.statement: Sensitive scope verification typically takes 3–5 business days.
claims.quote: The sensitive scope verification process typically takes 3-5 business days to complete.

claims.statement: Brand verification typically takes 2–3 business days after submission.
claims.quote: The brand verification process typically takes 2-3 business days after submission.

claims.statement: You must publish your branding before you can request data access verification.
claims.quote: Note that you must have a published branding status before you can request verification for data access.

claims.statement: A passing brand verification result is valid for 7 days.
claims.quote: Note: Compliant verification results are valid for 7 days.

claims.statement: If you don't publish within 7 days, the status changes to Need to re-verify and you must run brand verification again.
claims.quote: If you don't publish within that timeframe, the status will change to Need to re-verify and you will have to run the brand verification again.

claims.statement: An app in Testing is limited to 100 test users.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Cloud Help: Manage app audience
claims.quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.

claims.statement: A test user's authorization expires seven days after consent.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Cloud Help: Manage app audience
claims.quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent.

claims.statement: The app is In production after you select the Publish app button.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Cloud Help: Manage app audience
claims.quote: A project's publishing status is considered In production after selecting the Publish app button.

claims.statement: External apps are available to any user with a Google Account.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Cloud Help: Manage app audience
claims.quote: Projects configured with a user type of External are available to any user with a Google Account.

claims.statement: Users outside an Internal app's organization get an org_internal error.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Cloud Help: Manage app audience
claims.quote: An org_internal authorization error is displayed when authorization is requested from users outside the Google Cloud project's parent.

claims.statement: Unverified apps using sensitive or restricted scopes are capped at 100 new users.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Cloud Help: OAuth App Verification FAQ
claims.quote: To protect users and Google systems from abuse, unverified apps that are accessing restricted or sensitive scopes have a 100 new-user cap restriction.

claims.statement: The user cap covers the project's whole lifetime and can't be reset.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Cloud Help: Manage app audience
claims.quote: The user cap applies over the entire lifetime of the project, and it cannot be reset or changed.

claims.statement: Verify ownership of your authorized domains in Google Search Console.
claims.quote: Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console

claims.statement: Domain verification uses a Google account that is Owner or Editor on the project.
claims.quote: Use a Google Account that's associated with your API Console project as an Owner or an Editor.

claims.statement: The privacy policy must be on the same domain as the home page and linked from the consent screen.
claims.quote: The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page, and linked to on the OAuth consent screen of the Google API Console.

claims.statement: The home page must be publicly accessible.
claims.quote: Your home page must be publicly accessible, and not just accessible to your site's logged-in users.

claims.statement: Verification asks for a detailed justification and a video demonstration for sensitive scopes.
claims.quote: Submitting your app for verification involves confirming policy compliance, keeping contact information current, using the Cloud Console Verification Center, declaring all scopes, and providing detailed justification and a video demonstration for sensitive scopes.

claims.statement: The demo video is uploaded to YouTube Studio with visibility set to Unlisted.
claims.quote: Upload the video to YouTube Studio and set Visibility as Unlisted

claims.statement: The video must show the OAuth grant process users will see, in English.
claims.quote: Show the OAuth grant process that users will experience, in English.

claims.statement: Apps with both AI agent workflows and standard user features should use a separate OAuth client for each.
claims.quote: If your app supports both AI agent workflows and standard user features, create separate OAuth clients for each.

claims.statement: You create an OAuth client ID by choosing the app platform and filling in the required fields.
claims.quote: Create an OAuth client ID by choosing the correct app platform and filling the required fields.

claims.statement: A Google Workspace admin has the final say on whether an app can access their organization's data.
claims.quote: In essence, Google's verification process is a signal of general policy compliance, but the Google Workspace administrator has the ultimate authority on whether an app can access their organization's data.

claims.statement: If an app requests a restricted service and the admin hasn't trusted it, users can't add it.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Workspace Admin Help: Control which apps access Workspace data
claims.quote: While users are prompted to consent to apps, if an app requests access to a restricted service and you haven't specifically trusted the app, users can't add it.

claims.statement: Google charges no fee for the security assessment.
claims.sourceTitle: Google Cloud Help: OAuth App Verification FAQ
claims.quote: Google does not charge the developer any fees for security assessment.

claims.statement: Standard use of the Gmail API costs nothing extra.
claims.quote: All standard use of the Gmail API is available at no additional cost.

claims.statement: Google emails you when it's time to recertify.
claims.quote: The Google review team emails you when it is time to recertify your app.

claims.statement: Time to test (~1 hour), hands-on effort (2–4 days) and the overall timeline are estimates.
claims.note: Our estimates, built from Google's published review times (2–3, 3–5 business days; several weeks). Google publishes no end-to-end figure.
